newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares near records in early bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares near records in early bourse trade.

text.p: Germany's top share index opened bourse trade on Wednesday more than half a percentage point higher, lifted again by the strength of the U.S. dollar trading above 1.64 marks.

A positive close overnight on Wall Street also underpinned trade and the DAX index of 30 blue-chip stocks was up 21.11 points at 3,087.73 points at 1015 GMT, after earlier setting a new intraday record of 3,090.52 points.

"There is strong support there from the dollar and the focus is very much on individual stocks, although the chemical sector is strong because of the dollar. The specific interest this morning is on Lufthansa," said one trader.
Deutsche Lufthansa AG was one of the main gainers in early bourse trade, up 5.42 percent at 23.35 marks after the airline made a series of restructuring announcements.

Lufthansa said it would create autonomous profit centres and planned to create a separate division for passenger services from April 1 in addition to reducing management and administration by a minimum of 10 percent.
The group said the restructuring was in response to the April 1 liberalisation of the European airline industry.
The stronger dollar lifted chemical stocks, which were among the main leaders in early floor trade. The sector also saw significant volumes.
BASF AG was up 1.24 marks at 60.75 marks, Bayer AG was up 1.95 marks at 64.05 marks, while Hoechst AG was also strongly ahead, up 1.60 marks at 70.75 marks.
Shares in retailer Metro AG were up 90 pfennigs at 126.50 after the retailer said 1996 group sales were unchanged at 62 billion marks and it expected at least one billion marks in profit.
